originalGoal: Add a consistent retry policy to the TypeScript and Python SDKs. Specify retryable HTTP statuses (429 and 503), Retry-After handling, exponential backoff, maximum attempts and non-idempotent request protection in a new contracts/retry-policy.md before implementation. Implement and unit-test that contract in clients/typescript/client.ts and clients/python/client.py. Review both clients together and write reproducible conformance scenarios and results in tests/sdk-conformance.md, checking both use identical policy semantics. If that review finds nonconformance, request corrections to both client implementations and repeat the conformance review. Do not put retry behavior in the server or browser app.

nodes.name: retry-contract
nodes.task: Author contracts/retry-policy.md as the single authoritative cross-SDK retry contract for the Atlas client SDKs (clients/typescript/client.ts and clients/python/client.py). It must define, precisely enough that two independent implementers produce identical semantics: (1) retryable HTTP statuses = exactly 429 and 503 (state explicitly that other 4xx/5xx, including the 400/500 errors listed in contracts/users.json, are not retried); (2) Retry-After handling — precedence over backoff, accepted formats, units, clamping/invalid-value behavior; (3) exponential backoff — base delay, multiplier, growth formula, jitter policy, and cap; (4) maximum attempts — total-attempt vs retry-count semantics and default value; (5) non-idempotent request protection — which methods/requests are eligible for retry and how a non-idempotent request is protected; (6) behavior when retries are exhausted (error/exception surfaced) and any opt-out/configuration surface. Include a short normalization/conformance table of scenarios (status, headers, method) -> expected attempt counts and delays that both clients must satisfy. Keep it purely client-side: the contract must state that no retry behavior belongs in server/ or web/. Do not implement client code.

nodes.name: ts-client-retry
nodes.task: Implement the retry policy specified in contracts/retry-policy.md inside the TypeScript SDK at clients/typescript/client.ts, extending the existing Client class without changing its existing public behavior, and add unit tests (in the location/style used by the repo's existing tests, runnable via `npm test` / node --test) that prove every clause of the contract: only 429 and 503 retried, Retry-After precedence and format handling, exponential backoff values and cap/jitter rules, maximum-attempt accounting, non-idempotent request protection, and exhausted-retry error surfacing. Tests must not require live network or the running server. Report the exact command run and pass/fail counts. Do not modify contracts/retry-policy.md, clients/python/client.py, server/, or web/.

nodes.name: py-client-retry
nodes.task: Implement the same retry policy from contracts/retry-policy.md inside the Python SDK at clients/python/client.py, extending the existing Client class without changing its existing public behavior, and add unit tests that prove every clause of the contract: only 429 and 503 retried, Retry-After precedence and format handling, exponential backoff values and cap/jitter rules, maximum-attempt accounting, non-idempotent request protection, and exhausted-retry error surfacing. Tests must not require live network or the running server, and must be runnable with the project's available Python test entry point; report the exact command and pass/fail counts. Do not modify contracts/retry-policy.md, clients/typescript/client.ts, server/, or web/.

nodes.name: conformance-review
nodes.task: Perform an independent joint conformance review of clients/typescript/client.ts and clients/python/client.py against contracts/retry-policy.md, and write the result into tests/sdk-conformance.md (replacing its current placeholder text). For each contract clause, record a reproducible scenario (request method, response status, Retry-After value, expected attempts and delays), the exact command executed in each SDK, the real observed result/exit status, and a per-SDK pass/fail plus a verdict on whether both clients exhibit identical policy semantics. Also confirm no retry behavior was added to server/ or web/. Do not implement fixes. End with exactly one marker: <ACCEPT> if both clients fully conform and the recorded evidence is reproducible; <REVISE> otherwise, followed by a numbered list of specific nonconformities, each tagged TS and/or PY (tag both when the contract wording itself is ambiguous), naming the file and contract clause to correct.

nodes.name: final-verification
nodes.task: Give the final confirmation that the retry work is complete and correctly scoped after conformance was accepted. Run the TypeScript SDK test entry point and the Python SDK test entry point, record the exact commands, exit codes, and passing/failing counts; verify tests/sdk-conformance.md records a <ACCEPT> outcome consistent with the re-run evidence and that it documents identical policy semantics for both clients. Verify by inspection/search that retry logic exists only in clients/typescript/client.ts and clients/python/client.py (with contract in contracts/retry-policy.md) and that server/ and web/ contain no retry behavior. Report facts, evidence links, and explicit separation of observed evidence from inference.
